note: Read 2026-11-03 in the Revised Edition 2020 the Attorney General's Ministry publishes (agm.gov.bz). Majority and work: null here; the person research's majority (eighteen, the Interpretation Act's 'adult') and working age (twelve, the Labour Act, s. 169(a); a younger performer barred, the only exception, s. 171, being unpaid charitable entertainment) are read from that file (research/sources/person/ages/BZ.json, tools/papers/ages/person.ts), and today's reading of the same Acts found them unchanged: the Labour Act's 'child' is under fourteen, none employed under twelve, nor in an industrial undertaking (s. 164); the Families and Children Act's 'child' is under eighteen. Service: null. The Defence Act, s. 16(2), enlists no one under eighteen in the regular force, and s. 167(1) lets the Governor-General make regulations calling men out for national service; no such regulations were found (the game doesn't read service).

sources.title: Interpretation Act, Cap. 1, s. 3 (Substantive Laws of Belize, Revised Edition 2020, Attorney General's Ministry)
sources.said: “adult” means any person who has attained the age of eighteen years;

sources.title: Labour Act, Cap. 297 (Revised Edition 2020), ss. 2, 164, 169 and 171, Attorney General's Ministry
sources.said: “child” means a person who is under the age of fourteen years; ... 164.-(1) Subject to sub-section (2), no person shall employ a child in a public or private industrial undertaking or in a branch thereof. ... 169. Subject to any regulations made under section 170 no child shall be employed– (a) so long as he is under the age of twelve years; ... 171. Nothing in sections 170(1)(c) or 169(d) or in any regulations shall prevent a child from taking part without fee or reward in an entertainment, the net proceeds of which are devoted to any charitable or educational purpose or to any purpose other than the private profit of the promoters.

sources.title: Families and Children Act, Cap. 173 (Revised Edition 2020), Attorney General's Ministry
sources.said: “child” means, unless provided otherwise in any law, a person below the age of eighteen years;

sources.title: Defence Act, Cap. 135 (Revised Edition 2020), ss. 16(2) and 167(1), Attorney General's Ministry
sources.said: (2) A recruiting officer shall not enlist a person under the age of eighteen years in the regular force. ... 167.-(1) The Governor-General may, after consultation with the Prime Minister, make regulations providing for the calling out of men for national service.
